read_policy: read every cited file; validate against real code; declare read limits

rules.description: Domain/application layers reference infrastructure
Domain/application layers depend on a framework (only exception: org.springframework.stereotype.Service and org.springframework.transaction.annotation.* on application use cases; nothing in domain)
Dependency points outward
Use case depends on a concrete implementation instead of a port
Persistence entity or transport DTO used as domain model
Business logic in adapter or I/O in domain
External I/O interaction without a port (clock/random ids in domain are WARN unless they prevent deterministic tests)
Cyclic dependency between modules
Adapter depends directly on another adapter
No composition root (Spring: @SpringBootApplication class + component-scan; bootstrap package not required)
Port wider than 7 methods
Use case orchestrates more than one aggregate
Global static state or singletons
Technology name leaks into core naming

Framework in domain; Lombok/@Slf4j/@Autowired/web/persistence types in application; @Service allowed on application use cases and @Transactional only on multi-port write methods (INV-12/INV-18); Java/Spring-only exception
Lossy domain<->persistence mapping (INV-11)
Errors not translated at inbound boundary (INV-15)
Clock/random ids generated in domain preventing deterministic tests, or adapter generating business ids/setting clock (INV-13)

Disproportionate design: extra classes/layers that only duplicate a framework annotation or mechanism (BeanConfig, transactional decorators, needless mappers); ask the user instead of applying a skill rule blindly
Use case without inbound adapter (INV-14)

forbidden_in_core.description: Tokens (language-agnostic hints) that must never appear in domain/application layers
imports_patterns: org.springframework (application may only use org.springframework.stereotype.Service and org.springframework.transaction.annotation.*; domain none)
